subject: Dedicated throughput smoothing & queue-shaping proposal

Subject: Dedicated capacity: queueing & warmup behavior — request for smoothing clause

Hi Irene,

Thanks for running the performance run last week. A couple of things popped up on our side during the dedicated pool verification: when we switch traffic to the Dedicated pool there is a 5-20 minute window where tail latency jumps (mostly p95/p99) as caches populate and GPUs finish background kernel warmups. That transient behavior is fine operationally, but Procurement needs a clear contractual treatment for the first warmup window.

Specifically we're asking for one of the following:
- a defined "smoothing window" that explicitly allows measured ramp behavior (example: first 10 minutes have relaxed latency SLO but must not exceed 2x baseline p99), or
- a crediting model that compensates us for minutes above agreed SLO thresholds during the initial warm period, or
- explicit pre-warm steps that Redwood will run prior to cutover to eliminate the window.

Can you share Redwood's recommended language and any empirical numbers you have from similar customers? I've attached the test traces from our side (throughput-metrics.csv). Procurement would like to resolve this before we sign.

Alex

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear notes and for the csv. Marking Diego and Rishi to provide the tech + legal options.

High level: we absolutely understand the concern. We typically handle this three ways depending on the customer's risk appetite:
1) Pre-warm + synthetic traffic: we run a pre-warm job that loads model parameters & warms KV caches (reduces warmup from minutes to seconds).
2) Smoothing window: define a timeboxed ramp (e.g., 10 minutes) with an explicit latency bound relative to baseline (we can propose p95/p99 multipliers).
3) Credit/escrow: apply minute-level SLA credits for minutes where committed p95/p99 thresholds are exceeded during the first X minutes after cutover.

I'm attaching a short draft we put together for similar requests (queue-shaping-draft.pdf). Can Diego propose concrete operational steps and a suggested credit formula? Laura — once we have language, can you coordinate with Procurement and get the exact acceptance criteria?

Thanks,

Alex — digging into the test traces you sent, the pattern is consistent with cold KV cache population combined with a short kernel JIT warmup on some GPU stacks. Quick technical summary and mitigation options: 

Observed behavior:
- Baseline steady-state p95 ~ 120ms, p99 ~ 340ms.
- During initial traffic shift p95 spikes to ~350ms and p99 to ~1.1s for a 3–12 minute window depending on sequence length and concurrency.

Mitigation options (we can mix):
- Pre-warm pool: allocate a small warm pool of nodes (N small) and run synthetic requests to prepopulate model KV & kernels. This reduces ramp to <60s in most cases.
- Admission control (queue-shaping): during handover enforce a token-bucket at the routing layer to shape ingress so backend can steady-state without queue blowups. This keeps tail latency predictable but will reduce peak throughput during the window.
- Graceful fallback: keep a hosted-compatible model variant available (lower-cost variant or smaller context) to absorb overflow while Dedicated warms. Requests that exceed a configured latency threshold can be redirected.
- Credit formula: we recommend a linear minute-credit: credit_minutes = max(0, minutes_exceeding_SLO - smoothing_allowance) * (commitment_rate_per_minute * credit_pct). Example in attachment.

Operational proposal for Skylife Net:
1) 10-minute smoothing window by default.
2) Redwood runs pre-warm job starting 5 minutes before cutover (ops-triggered).
3) Admission control cap to constrain burst to 3x baseline QPS for first 10 minutes.
4) If p99 > 2x baseline for more than smoothing allowance, apply credit at 1.5x the per-minute rate for minutes over threshold (example calculation in sla-redline.docx).

If that sounds reasonable I'll produce a tight contract paragraph and the exact metric math.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head of Runtime Product
Redwood Inference

Irene/Diego — thanks for the clear options, Diego. Procurement is willing to accept a timeboxed smoothing window, but with two conditions:
1) The smoothing window must not allow p99 to exceed 2x baseline beyond the stated allowance. If it does, credits must apply automatically (we need the formula in the contract).
2) The smoothing procedure must include a documented pre-warm step (who initiates, runbook steps, rollback triggers).

A couple clarifying Qs:
- Can Redwood guarantee that pre-warm will be executed as an automated step (we'd prefer an API trigger we can call during cutover)?
- In the admission control option, what's the expected throughput reduction (percent) during a 10-minute window? We need a worst-case number for procurement modeling.

I'll review the examples in sla-redline.docx and loop procurement in once we have the exact clause and the DocuSign ready.

Alex

Alex — appreciate the quick feedback. I have drafted proposed contract language (see attached sla-redline.docx) that implements Diego's operational plan and includes an automated pre-warm API trigger. A few notes: 

- Pre-warm will be available as an API call (POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/prewarm) that your ops team can call as part of cutover. Redwood can also run it as a managed step if you prefer.
- We conservatively estimate throughput reduction during the 10-minute admission-control window at ~20–35% depending on concurrency and request distribution; worst-case we model 40% for Procurement planning. We'll include that as the worst-case number.
- Credit formula in the redline uses the per-minute commitment rate in your order form; credits are applied automatically if measured minutes over threshold > smoothing_allowance.

Next steps:
1) Alex — confirm you want the API pre-warm or managed pre-warm (we can include both options).
2) If yes, I'll push the redline to DocuSign and tag DL-2026-1189.
3) Diego & Rishi — please confirm the 40% worst-case guidance and if you want a different multiplier for longer sequences.
